scope: Theorem 7.1 (Finite-data Frobenius incompatibility) of the manuscript “Fourfold nonvanishing by minimal metrics and moving jets” (preprints/Fourfold-nonvanishing-by-minimal-metrics-and-moving-jets-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1946d50201ab1ae0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let W be a smooth connected projective complex variety of dimension n ≥ 2. Fix rational Cartier divisors L, H, with H ample, an integral Cartier divisor S, an integer q > 0, and real numbers r > 1, ϵ > 0. Suppose Hn ≤ (2ϵ)n , KW Hn−1 ≤ 2Hn /r, (2L + qS)Hn−1 ≤ 4Hn , (14ϵ)n < 1/4, 80ϵ < 3/4. The following three kinds of fixed data cannot all exist. (i) A smooth integral complete-intersection flag ending in a curve C, of successive divisor classes liH for positive integers li, with µmin(Ω1 W |C) ≥ 0. (ii) On ZW = P(O(S)1 ⊕ O(S)2) → W × W, in the symmetric-power convention, put M = L1 + L2 + qξ. For some integer k0 > 0 with k0L Cartier, finitely many sections of k0M surject onto OZW ,z∗ /m (2n+2)k0+1 z∗ after trivialization at a smooth torus point z∗. (iii) A point x ∈ W, the blowup πx : c W → W with exceptional divisor Jx, and a curve class γ = f∗(A1 · · · An−1), where f : V → c W is a fixed birational morphism from a smooth integral projective variety and the Ai are ample Cartier divisors, such that Jxγ > 0 and π∗ x(L + KW /2 + λS)γ ≤ 40ϵJxγ (0 ≤ λ ≤ q). It suffices to check the two endpoint inequalities. No nefness of L, S, KW is assumed, and z∗ need not lie over x. All divisors, the flag, the point, the curve representative, and the finite jet sections are fixed over C before the residual characteristic varies.
